messages:
olivia: customer reports 401 `invalid_api_key` right after rotating a key. They say their JS SDK started failing in prod behind a small auth proxy. stack: react native app -> auth-proxy -> our hosted api. examples pasted below.

kevin: can you paste the raw Authorization header from the failing request?

olivia: pasted from the proxy logs: `Authorization: ApiKey ApiKey sk_live_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`

kevin: oof — looks like the proxy is already adding `ApiKey ` and our SDK also prefixes when set to send raw key. double prefix is why server rejects. server expects either `ApiKey <key>` or bare key in X-API-Key header depending on client method. our auth layer canonicalizer rejects any token that doesn't match /^sk_\w{24,}/ (it sees the extra `ApiKey ` and fails).

olivia: repro curl I gave them to confirm:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: ApiKey ApiKey sk_live_XXXX" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings
```

api-bot: quick check: key sk_live_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX status=active scope=hosted, last_used=2026-02-28T10:12:34Z, region=us-west-2 (no server-side revoke).

ingrid: suggested fixes: 1) stop proxy from injecting `ApiKey ` if upstream already sends it, 2) set SDK config to send bare header `X-Api-Key: <key>` (sdk option: authMode: "headerBare"), or 3) remove prefix in proxy with small rewrite rule.

kevin: also note we recently tightened validation to prevent duplicated auth schemes (security audit). servers will now return 401 with `invalid_api_key` when header contains non-key prefix. that's working-as-intended.

olivia: passed both fixes to customer. they confirmed removing prefix in proxy fixed it immediately. new request header is `Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` and calls succeed.

kevin: adding a short troubleshooting note to our docs: "If you see `ApiKey ApiKey` in logs, remove duplicate prefix (proxy or SDK)". small PR upcoming. :memo:

olivia: closing the thread with customer confirmation. :white_check_mark:
